newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore blue chips, IPO's return to favour early.
newsitem.headline: Singapore blue chips, IPO's return to favour early.

text.p: Investor interest in Singapore blue chip stocks and some newly launched issues perked early on Friday as momentum in Malaysian counters sobered, dealers said.
"The Singapore side is firming while Malaysia is stalling. People are tending to close out profits," a dealer with a local securities house said.
Recent heavy trading in Malaysian Clob counters was likely to continue but at a slower pace ahead of the weekend, he said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index was up 0.98 points to 2,264.66 at 0210 GMT, and turnover was a brisk 140 million shares after just over an hour of trade.
On Thursday, Singapore $1.27 billion worth of shares and warrants changed hands, marking the first time in just over a year that daily volume crossed the billion dollar level.
Dealers said that speculative trading following the upward re-rating of the Singapore bourse.
Top gainers were the Asean Fund, up S$0.50 to S$18.70, Orchard Parade, up S$0.30 at $4.00 and the foreign tranche of DBS, up S$0.20 at $20.00.
IPO's dominated actives with vegetable and fruit supplier FHTK up three cents at S$0.69, and Chuan Soon Huat up three cents at S$0.58.
